subject: food-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which group of nutrients is classed as the macronutrients?
questions.explain: Macronutrients are carbohydrate, protein and fat because they are needed by the body in relatively large amounts.

questions.q: Which two types of nutrient make up the micronutrients?
questions.explain: Micronutrients are vitamins and minerals, which the body requires only in small amounts.

questions.q: Why are vitamins and minerals described as micronutrients?
options: They are needed by the body only in small amounts
They provide most of the body's energy
They cannot be stored in the body
They are only found in fruit and vegetables
questions.explain: The prefix 'micro' reflects that these nutrients are essential but required in only very small quantities.

questions.q: What is the main function of carbohydrate in the diet?
options: To provide the body with energy
To build and repair body cells
To help the blood to clot
questions.explain: Carbohydrate is the body's main and most readily available source of energy.

questions.q: Which nutrient is mainly needed for the growth and repair of body cells?
questions.explain: Protein is essential for the growth, repair and maintenance of body tissues.

questions.q: Which food is the best source of high biological value (HBV) protein?
questions.explain: Eggs, like most animal foods, provide HBV protein because they contain all the essential amino acids.

questions.q: Why is it useful to eat a food rich in vitamin C at the same time as an iron-rich meal?
options: Vitamin C helps the body to absorb iron
Vitamin C turns iron into calcium
Vitamin C prevents iron being stored
questions.explain: Vitamin C aids the absorption of iron, particularly non-haem iron from plant foods.

questions.q: Which vitamin helps the body to absorb calcium?
questions.explain: Vitamin D is needed for the absorption of calcium, which is required for strong bones and teeth.

questions.q: A lack of iron in the diet over time is most likely to lead to which condition?
questions.explain: Iron is needed to form haemoglobin, so a deficiency can result in iron-deficiency anaemia.

questions.q: Calcium is important in the diet mainly because it helps to:
options: Insulate the body against the cold
questions.explain: Calcium is a key mineral for the formation and maintenance of strong bones and teeth.

questions.q: Which group correctly lists the fat-soluble vitamins?
questions.explain: Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat-soluble, whereas the B group and vitamin C are water-soluble.

questions.q: A prolonged lack of vitamin C in the diet is most likely to cause:
questions.explain: Vitamin C is needed for healthy connective tissue, and a severe deficiency causes scurvy.

questions.q: The energy provided by food and used by the body is measured in:
questions.explain: Food energy is measured in kilocalories (kcal) and kilojoules (kJ).

questions.q: Which nutrient provides the most energy per gram?
questions.explain: Fat provides about 9 kcal per gram, more than double that of carbohydrate or protein.

questions.q: What is the likely result if a person's energy intake is regularly greater than their energy output?
options: Their weight will stay the same
questions.explain: When energy in exceeds energy out, the surplus is stored as body fat and weight increases.

questions.q: Basal metabolic rate (BMR) is best described as the energy needed to:
options: Keep the body's vital functions working at rest
questions.explain: BMR is the amount of energy required to maintain essential body functions, such as breathing and circulation, at rest.

questions.q: A portion of food contains 20 g of fat. Using 9 kcal per gram, how much energy does the fat provide?
questions.explain: 20 g of fat multiplied by 9 kcal per gram equals 180 kcal.

questions.q: A teenager has been told to increase their iron intake. Which food should they choose?
questions.explain: Red meat is a rich source of readily absorbed haem iron.

questions.q: A person wants to lose weight safely. Which change would best help them to achieve a negative energy balance?
options: Eat fewer high-energy foods and be more physically active
Eat more fatty foods and rest more
Skip all meals for several days
Drink more sugary drinks before exercise
questions.explain: Reducing energy intake while increasing energy output creates a negative energy balance, leading to gradual weight loss.

questions.q: A meal of grilled chicken with a jacket potato provides protein and starchy carbohydrate. Which macronutrient supplies the starchy carbohydrate?
questions.explain: Potatoes are a starchy food and therefore the main source of carbohydrate in the meal, while chicken supplies protein.
